title: DeckCraft placed-plant realism, revised after review. Fix the render and the beds first, gate every phase on a measured performance probe, then add project-owned species models, ranked by how often each plant is used times how wrong it looks today. Plan only; awaiting owner approval.
thesis:
Most of what looks fake today comes from the render path and the beds, not the meshes. The canvas is created with alpha:true, so the page shows through every alpha-to-coverage leaf edge; the magenta test proved it. Leaves are glossy and their albedo is lifted, the proxy plants are squashed, plants in plain beds are buried 3.05 in under a raised, flat, constant-orange mulch slab, and steel edging stands 7 in above grade.

The plan therefore opens with three render-only PRs. Data, prices, share links and exports stay byte-identical.
- **P0:** an opaque canvas, plus a probe that gates every later phase. It measures draws, triangles, texture MiB, overdraw and frame time on each desktop tier and on the owner's iPhone.
- **P1:** honest, matte foliage.
- **P2:** plants seated in beds. Mulch sits just below the grass tips with a spade-cut taper. Each plant gets a soil collar with a mulch lip, plus contact shade sized to its form. Edging is near-flush and mulch colours are honest.

After that, the shared proxies are replaced by project-owned procedural species models. A model is chosen at render time from speciesRecord.id, with the saved assetId as the fallback. The waves are ranked by estate count times wrongness:
1. Clipped evergreens.
2. Herbaceous plants.
3. Shrubs.
4. Perennials.
5. Deciduous trees.
6. Conifers.

The models are built in the repo from botany specs and from CC0-derived detail tiles. The tiles are committed, so CI and Netlify never touch the network.

Each wave is gated by contact sheets, screenshots at named cameras and Node checks: LOD silhouette and edge, colour (ΔE00 ≤ 5 plus species ordering), triangles and draws. The browser frame-time probe gates each wave too.

At the triangle caps:
- The estate showcase drops from 2.52M to about 0.84M triangles.
- The constrained estate stays under 45k triangles.
- Plant texture memory on the high tier falls from about 34 MiB to about 12.4 MiB.
- All 15 legacy GLBs stay byte-identical.
- No CC BY asset, KTX2, paid asset or new runtime dependency is used.

Sizing new placements at installed versus mature size is a separate, optional last phase. Changing PLANT_LIBRARY envelopes only affects newly placed plants, and the estate generator overrides several of them anyway.

work:

- Still export encodes the canvas with toBlob (SceneStillExport.tsx:26).
- The fly-through recorder and the primed and fallback frames (renderPipeline.tsx:149-171) render to the canvas.

The earlier OutputPass patch and its source assertion are dropped, which costs no viewer-chunk bytes.
**Keep alphaToCoverage** at Landscape3D.tsx:57. Without the leak it gives clean antialiased leaf edges.

**Fixture.** scripts/fixtures/plants-realism-demo.json holds DEFAULT_DECK plus the 31-plant, 26-species demo bed from docs/deckcraft/plants-realism-2026-10-17/demo-planting.json (untracked, main checkout only). It is rearranged so that bed seating can be seen:
- Red maple (single trunk) and serviceberry (multi-stem) move into the front third of the bed (z 222-258) at its two ends, with nothing taller in front of them. The front-row perennials they displace shift one slot inward.
- Dogwood (open, red-stem base) swaps into the front row with a low perennial.
- Sugar maple, redbud, white pine and blue spruce stay on the lawn at z 420 as lawn-tree subjects.
- The docs copy is not edited.

**Cameras**, saved as presentation cameras in the fixture:
- Bed close-up: eye 60 in high, 120 in in front of the bed centre, aimed 18 in high, fov 38.
- Bed edge low: eye 30 in, looking along the bed's long front edge.
- Plant base macro: eye about 30 in, about 4 ft from the red maple trunk, with the dogwood base in frame.
- Tree in lawn: eye about 30 in, about 5 ft from the sugar maple trunk on the lawn.
Corner, Overview, Front and Above are also used.

**Forced tiers without a src change.** A Playwright init script spoofs WEBGL_debug_renderer_info UNMASKED_RENDERER, navigator.deviceMemory and hardwareConcurrency:
- A SwiftShader string gives constrained.
- 4 GB and 4 cores give balanced.
- The real GPU with 8 GB and 8 cores gives high.
A 390x844 viewport gives narrow. chooseRenderQuality (renderQuality.ts:10-18) is untouched.

**Probe without a src change.** The init script defines window.__THREE_DEVTOOLS__ as an EventTarget before the 3D view opens. three 0.185.1 then announces its WebGLRenderer and Scenes in the production build (WebGLRenderer.js:3569, Scene.js:115). The probe, scripts/plants-probe/probe.js:
- Sets gl.info.autoReset=false and resets once per rAF frame. three resets renderer.info on every render() call, so a read after the frame would show only the last full-screen quad.
- Wraps gl.render and renderBufferDirect, following the releaseDrawnResources pattern. It counts draws and triangles per pass: beauty, each window-reflection pass, shadow map, ground occlusion and post.
- Counts as 'plant draws' only meshes named /^landscape-.+-lod[0-2]$/. Contact decals and bed bands are counted separately.
- Computes texture MiB from the bound textures (width × height × bytes per texel × 4/3 when mipmapped), grouped as plant, contact decal or other.
- Records gl.info.programs.length, and the longest frame in the 2 s after the 1.2 s LOD switch.
- Counts shadow-map redraws and logs the sun shadow camera's extent and texel size.

**Frame time.** A 10 s synthetic pointer-drag orbit on the canvas at Corner and Front, on the estate and the demo, at each forced tier on the owner's GPU. It records p50 and p95 rAF intervals, and GPU ms through EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 where the browser exposes it.
**Overdraw.** An additive override material on plant meshes at Front and Bed close-up, read back as mean fragments per covered pixel, per tier.

**iPhone run.** scripts/serve-plants-probe.mjs serves the local production build on a free LAN port in the 4000-4099 build range, checked before binding.
- It injects the probe into HTML responses on that server only, so the deployed site never contains it.
- The probe overlays p50/p95, a context-loss count and the tier.
- The owner opens it on the iPhone in portrait (balanced), runs the orbit and screenshots the overlay.

**Capture harness.** scripts/capture-plants-realism.ts follows the capture-photo-stills.ts pattern. It covers:
- Scenes: the demo and the estate.
- All cameras, at 1600x900 and 390x844.
- Day and Golden hour, with Realistic look off and on.
- The three forced tiers.
It writes PNGs plus metrics.json to docs/deckcraft/plants-realism-2026-10-17/p0/:
- Magenta probe: page background #f0f; count the canvas pixels with R>=200, G<=80, B>=200.
- Canopy crops, with the boxes logged: the placed sugar maple's mean canopy luminance against the nearest context tree (same GLB); % of canopy pixels above sRGB 235.
- Everything the probe records, per tier, scene and camera.
- First-paint and resize frames, captured right after mount and right after a resize.
**Node baseline.** Also recorded in metrics.json: the coverInstances time for the estate's largest bed at the high budget, used by the P2 timing check.

phases.name: Plants sit in beds
phases.goal: Plants sit in the mulch with their stems clear. Mulch sits just below the grass tips and tapers to grade like a spade cut. Edging sits nearly flush, mulch colours are honest, and every plant gets a contact cue sized to its form on every tier. All of this is render-only: quantities, exports, links, prices, picking and selection behave exactly as before.
work:
**Visual plateau (D8).** Non-raised mulch and aggregate beds render a viewer-only top sheet at grade + 1.0 in, below the lawn tuft tips (1.3-2.4 in tall, lawnTufts.ts:21-22). Today the sheet is at grade + 3.05 in.
- Real Ontario beds finish about level with the lawn, with mulch at the cut about 25 mm below the turf (Waterloo CW-711). They do not stand as a slab 3 in above it.
- mulchDepthIn, landscapeSurfaceDepth, the takeoff, landscapeBedGeometry and the designExports bed y are unchanged, so quantities and OBJ/DXF exports are identical.

**plantSeat** (new plantSeating.ts, lazy and Node-safe). plantSeat(data, o) returns:
- In an enabled non-raised bed: the rendered surface at the plant minus a per-form sink. The rendered surface is the plateau, or the band height within 4 in of a banded outline segment. Bed membership uses the same landscapeBedAreas polygons that Beds renders, not the outline-only raisedSupport rule. Those polygons apply fillSeed ordering and the seed-connected region, and clip out pools and, for groundCoverOnly beds, structures.
- In a raised bed: the landscapePlacement y minus the sink.
- On lawn: grade.

**Per-form values (D8).** A render table keyed by species form, with the asset form as the fallback:
- Trees: sink 0, mulch pulled back 3 in beyond the base radius.
- Shrubs and hull evergreens: sink 0.5 in, pull-back 2 in.
- Perennials and grasses: sink 0.75 in, pull-back 1.5 in.
Base radius defaults until P3 (after that, the species spec field baseRadiusIn from the generated stem cluster at y=0):
- Tree: 1.25 in, for a 2.5 in caliper.
- Multi-stem tree: 4 in.
- Shrub: 0.15 × widthIn, capped at 6 in.
- Perennial and grass: 0.2 × widthIn, capped at 4 in.

**Seat wiring.**
- The seat is premultiplied in InstancePart, so landscapeInstanceMatrix is unchanged.
- The PlantBlooms anchors (plantBlooms.tsx:111) and the MatureSpread ring (Landscape3D.tsx:89) also use plantSeat.
- landscapePlacement and its other callers are untouched: landscapeEdits.ts:31 and Deck3DViewer.tsx:661.

**Mulch colour.** In landscapeSurfaceMaterial.ts, patch key 'mulch-shred-fiber-v3':
- Albedo = linear(swatch) × fibre modulation (normalised to mean 1.0) × clamp(scanLuma / meanScanLuma, 0.6, 1.4).
- Swatches: brown #73503a, black #34302b, cedar #a97548.
- The swatch is a per-material uniform set when the material is created, so brown, black and cedar can share one program without sharing a colour. The loadPhotos completion callback updates the swatch and meanScanLuma on every material in resource.materials, which stays correct during the procedural DataTexture fallback.
- The shader divides out material.color, so the pinned multipliers (#ffffff, #2a2622, #ffce99) stay.
- The SurfaceDetail.tsx:35 chip colours derive from the same swatches.
- photoMaterials gives mulch beds the same albedo in the trace; today it has none.

**Bed edge** (new bedEdgeGeometry.ts, viewer-only), for non-raised mulch and aggregate beds.
Top sheet:
- Built from the landscapeBedAreas polygons at the plateau.
- Inset by 4 in only along banded segments. It runs to the outline on segments that have no band: shared with another enabled bed, or within 3 in of a house, deck, patio or wall footprint. That leaves no strip of bare lawn ground against a foundation or between beds.
Taper band:
- Runs from the outline at grade + 0.4 in up to the inset line at the plateau, following the TIN.
- Split at TIN triangle edges, and kept at least 0.25 in above the sampled ground.
- Sits entirely above grade, because the lawn ground mesh runs on under beds (groundDisplayCuts excludes beds).
- Its lower third is vertex-coloured soil (#3b2f25), which reads as the spade-cut line.
Both meshes:
- uv1 is built from occlusionUv.
- They carry the bed's pick metadata, {pickPartId:'landscape/'+id, landscapeIds:[id]}, so clicks on the sheet or the band select the bed.
- The band has its own userData flag, never renderOnly, because photoSkip hides renderOnly meshes in traced stills.
Unchanged: landscapeBedGeometry, landscapeCellTriangles and designExports. Raised, turf and putting-green beds keep their current geometry.

**Steel edging.**
- Only when raisedBedTop is undefined, Bed passes the ribbon base at grade - 3.5 in, so the unchanged steelEdgingGeometry (4 in rise) tops out at grade + 0.5 in. Raised-bed edging keeps its on-top placement.
- Edging segments are split at TIN triangle edges, as the band is, so a 0.5 in reveal neither sinks nor floats mid-span on a sloped TIN.
- Material: the raised-bed weathered steel (#4a3b32, roughness .78), per D9.
- With edging on, the band's outer edge sits within 0.25 in of the edging top.

**Soil collar and mulch lip** (new plantContactDecals.tsx), for bed plants only.
Soil collar:
- One InstancedMesh of opaque, lit, irregular 14-gon soil discs (#3b2f25 with vertex noise).
- Radius: base radius + the per-form pull-back.
- y is the rendered bed surface at the plant + 0.04 in, never the sunk seat, so it cannot hide under the sheet. polygonOffset is applied.
Mulch lip:
- A second InstancedMesh: an annulus 1.75 in wide in the bed's mulch material.
- It rises from the surface at its outer edge to +0.6 in at its inner edge, so the soil reads as a dip whose rim catches light.
Both meshes:
- Opaque with no alpha, so the path tracer traces them as they are.
- raycast is a no-op and userData.coversGround is false.

**AO ring** (plantContactDecals.tsx), for every placed plant, on beds and on lawn.
- One InstancedMesh with an unlit radial texture. The texture is built lazily inside the component, so the module top level stays DOM-free: 256 px on high and balanced, 128 px on constrained.
- Material: MultiplyBlending with premultipliedAlpha:true and a premultiplied texture. three 0.185 leaves the blend state undefined otherwise (WebGLState.js:686-688).
- Sizing by form:
  - Foliage-to-ground forms (shrubs, hedges, hull evergreens, perennials, grasses, hosta, fern): radius 0.45 × widthIn, capped at 30 in.
  - Trees and multi-stem trees: base radius + 10 in. Canopy shade is left to shadows and the aoMap.
- Tilted to the local grade slope, with depthWrite false and polygonOffset -2.
- Strength scales with sun and ambient, so night does not show a stain.
- Drawn on every tier, including constrained.
- raycast is a no-op and coversGround is false.
- userData.photoSkip = true, so photoMaterials.tuneMaterial (:394) does not turn it into an opaque cutout; the tracer computes its own contact shade.

**Contact shade (D10a).** Non-raised bed materials take the shared GroundOcclusion texture as aoMap through uv1, as lawnSurface and finishedGrade already do.
- No new shadow casters: LOD2 plants still do not cast. This keeps fitSun's frustum and the house and deck shadow texel density as they are.
- groundOcclusion.ts and shadowCache.ts are not edited.

**Chips.** groundCoverDetail.ts and SurfaceDetail.tsx keep mulch chips clear of the 4 in band and of every collar and lip.
- A per-bed spatial hash of collars is built once per data change, so the per-chip test is O(1). Today coverInstances reruns on every 3 ft camera move with up to 65,000 chips.

**Fixture and capture.**
- Add three side-by-side beds (brown, black, cedar), one with edging on.
- Capture the p2/ set, including Above, Bed edge low, Plant base macro and Tree in lawn, on all three tiers, plus Night.

- Botany citations.
- Reference envelope and crown form.
- Stems and baseRadiusIn.
- Leaf or scale size in cm.
- Colour target: hue and chroma from the photo statistics; linear luminance from a per-class foliage-albedo band. Photo pixels are lit and white-balanced, so they are never used as albedo. owner_decisions.question: D1: Approve the plan and its order?
owner_decisions.options:
(a) Fix first (P0 canvas plus harness, P1 foliage, P2 beds), then the species waves ranked by estate count × wrongness:
- P3 Smaragd, boxwood, yew.
- P4 grasses, hosta, daylily, fern.
- P5 broadleaf shrubs.
- P6 flowering perennials.
- P7 deciduous trees.
- P8 conifers.
Then P9 hardening and the optional P10 sizes.
(a') The same, but ship the one-line canvas fix as its own tiny PR (P0a) before the harness (P0b).
(b) The same as (a), but trees (P7-P8) right after P3.
(c) Only P0-P2 for now.
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a). Use (a') if you want the speckle gone within hours rather than after the 1.5-day harness. P1 already removes the worst tree defects (gloss, lift, z-squash), so trees can wait until the pipeline is proven.

owner_decisions.question: D2: Several foliage terms never render in the live view, because they are added after outgoingLight is summed. Photo mode applies them anyway. They are the translucency, warm-highlight and shade-fill terms, plus the bloom lift. What should happen?
owner_decisions.options:
(a) In P1, delete them in both the raster shader and photoMaterials, so photo matches live, and add a bloom-card parity case. The live view does not change.
(b) Also, from P3, make translucency live for species materials only:
- Appended after '#include <lights_fragment_begin>' with its own getShadow for light 0.
- Divided by pi and thickness-weighted.
- Mirrored in photoMaterials.
- Judged on golden-hour before/after shots at the P3 gate.
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a) now. Decide (b) at the P3 gate from the screenshots, and keep it off unless backlit leaves are clearly better and show no glow.

owner_decisions.question: D3: Are procedural SVG sprites, preview contact sheets and any baked LOD or billboard images deterministic build-code output, rather than 'image generation' under the browser-flow approval rule?
owner_decisions.options:
(a) Yes: code output, reproducible from the spec table and the committed inputs by plants:verify, with no AI model involved.
(b) No: route them through a separate browser image-generation approval.

owner_decisions.question: D4: Where does species leaf, needle and flower detail come from?
owner_decisions.options:
(a) Procedural SVG botanical masks filled with contrast-limited, high-pass luminance detail tiles (mean 1.0), derived from approved CC0 iNaturalist photo crops, plus a venation overlay and edge noise.
- Photos supply hue and chroma only. Luminance comes from per-class albedo bands.
- Raw photos stay in a cache outside the repo and are never committed or shipped.
- The small derived tiles (at most 40 KB each) and colour statistics are committed under scripts/plant-species/inputs/ with provenance, so builds and CI work offline. CC0 allows this.
(b) Pure SVG, with photos used only to measure colour targets. Nothing photo-derived is committed or shipped, and the look risks being vector-clean.
(c) CC0 photogrammetry bakes (ffishAsia via Sketchfab): large owner-performed downloads and manual cut-outs.
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a). It avoids the vector-clean look at Bed close-up, stays CC0-only, keeps downloads small and keeps CI offline.

owner_decisions.question: D5: Accept CC BY 4.0 assets?
owner_decisions.options:
(a) No CC BY in this plan.
(b) PlantCatalog blue spruce Koster 12/43 only (57,131,704 B; CC BY 4.0, 'Commercial use is allowed', official e-on account). This adds:
- An owner-performed Sketchfab download, verified by sha256.
- Check-enforced attribution fields {title, author, sourceURL, licenceURL, changes}.
- CREDITS.html.
The maksm Spiraea japonica model is not offered. Its description says it was made for the University of Ljubljana APPLAUSE / 3D Virtual Wood Collection 'For educational purposes only', which conflicts with commercial use on a public business site. It stays blocked unless the owner obtains written commercial-use clearance from the author. The owner contacts authors; the agent drafts the message only if asked.
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a). The procedural pipeline covers all 26 species, and this keeps accounts, outreach and attribution UI off the critical path.

owner_decisions.options:
(a) Mid-July summer:
- Spring bloomers (redbud, serviceberry, lilac) in leaf, with seed heads or pods.
- Annabelle white; Karl Foerster plumes tan.
- Summer perennials in bloom.
(b) Add spring bloom states, which needs a viewer toggle.
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a). Seasonal states are out of scope.

owner_decisions.question: D8: Bed seating and bed-height values (render-only)?
owner_decisions.options:
Recommended:
- Visual plateau of non-raised mulch and aggregate beds at grade + 1.0 in (range 0.75-1.25), below the lawn tuft tips. mulchDepthIn, the takeoff and exports are unchanged.
- Sink below the rendered surface: trees 0; shrubs and hull evergreens 0.5 in; perennials and grasses 0.75 in.
- Mulch pulled back beyond the base radius: trees 3 in; shrubs 2 in; perennials and grasses 1.5 in.
- A soil collar at the surface, with a 1.75 in mulch lip rising 0.6 in, so the pull-back reads as a dip.
- Stems authored 2 in below the soil line, nothing more than 4 in below it, and no leaf part below -0.5 in.
- A 4 in taper down to grade + 0.4 in.
- Edging top at grade + 0.5 in.
Alternatives:
- Keep the true-thickness plateau at grade + 3.05 in (reads as a raised mulch pad).
- A single 0.75 in sink with a 2.5 in collar.
- Plants exactly on the surface.
owner_decisions.recommendation: The recommended values. They match the Toronto, Oshawa, Mississauga and Waterloo details: mulch about 25 mm below turf at the cut, flare at or just above grade, mulch held 40-75 mm off stems, and edging about 1/2 in proud.

owner_decisions.options:

(b) Black powder-coat.
(c) Mill aluminium.
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a). The quote note 'steel ribbon' stays true, and both bed types match.

owner_decisions.question: D10: How far should contact shade go?
owner_decisions.options:
(a) Beds take the existing shared GroundOcclusion texture as aoMap, plus the P2 decals on every tier. No new shadow casters: LOD2 plants still do not cast, so the sun's shadow frustum and the house and deck shadow sharpness stay as they are. groundOcclusion.ts and shadowCache.ts are not edited.
(b) Also make LOD2 plants cast on the high tier, and change fitSun (shadowCache.ts) to fit only non-plant casters plus LOD0/LOD1 plants, so the frustum does not widen.
(c) Also admit every plant LOD on every tier into the occlusion cover pass (userData.occludesSky). This edits groundOcclusion.ts in the viewer chunk and darkens lawn under phone-tier plants, which is a lawn look change.
(d) Decals only.
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a). Decals already cover far plants and the constrained tier. (b) and (c) wait for a later lawn or shadow phase.

owner_decisions.question: D11: Put the plant checks in the deploy gate, and how do they stay offline?
owner_decisions.options:
(a) Add checks to check:deck as each phase lands:
- check:landscape.
- check-landscape-surfaces, check-ground-cover-detail, check-curved-landscape-editing.
- check-plant-foliage (P1) and check-bed-edges (P2).
- check-plant-species and plants:verify (P3).
Also add public/deckcraft/** and scripts/plant-species/** to the deckcraft-e2e path filter.
The offline rule:
- plants:verify rebuilds geometry exactly and atlas pixels within tolerance from committed derived inputs only.
- It stubs fetch, http and https and fails on any network call.
- It fails above 120 s.
- No CI job, Netlify build or check script ever fetches from iNaturalist, S3 or Poly Haven.
- fetch-sources.mjs runs only on the owner's machine after each phase's dry-run approval.
This adds about 60-90 s to lint and the Netlify build.
(b) Keep the checks manual.
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a). Today an asset-only PR runs no GLB, licence or bed check. The offline rule means production deploys never depend on third-party sites or on an observer later changing a photo licence.

owner_decisions.question: D12: How are the generated plant assets labelled in species-manifest.json and ATTRIBUTION.md?
owner_decisions.options:
(a) A new label: 'Project-owned, derived from CC0-1.0 inputs', with per-input provenance.
- It is modelled on, not copied from, original-furniture-manifest.json. That file says 'Project-owned original assets; no external license or attribution dependency' and declares no third-party input.
- The repo has no LICENSE file, so the published outputs default to all rights reserved, which (a) intends.
(b) Dedicate the outputs CC0-1.0.

owner_decisions.question: D13: Promote meshoptimizer to an explicit devDependency?
owner_decisions.options:
(a) Yes: 1.1.1, already in node_modules and package-lock via @types/three, so no new download is expected.
(b) Use the transitive copy.
(c) Write uncompressed float32 GLBs.
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a). The decoder chunk already ships (5.1 KB gzip), so the runtime cost is zero.

owner_decisions.question: D14: Texture delivery?
owner_decisions.options:
(a) Shared WebP atlases (RGBA8), content-hashed and sized by tier. Build-time coverage-preserving mip strips only if the P3 spike passes on the owner's iPhone Safari; otherwise generated mips plus the P1 shader mip-alpha scale. The spike uses Chrome, Edge and the iPhone. Playwright WebKit (an extra 62.7 MB browser download) is not used unless approved.
(b) KTX2 now: about 29 KB of lazy loader JS plus a 245 KB self-hosted wasm, and the sharp-based checks must change.
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a). Revisit KTX2 only if the P9 measurements miss the budgets.

owner_decisions.question: D15: The proxy fern renders flat brown today. Fix it early?
owner_decisions.options:
(a) Wait for the procedural ostrich fern in P4. No download, and all 15 legacy GLBs stay frozen.
(b) P1 stop-gap: download Poly Haven fern_02_alpha_1k.png (114,589 B, CC0) and merge it into the three fern-clump GLBs with a new script. This unfreezes 3 legacy pins; build-plant-library-v2.mjs is never edited.

owner_decisions.question: D16: Caching for species files (a deploy-config change, in P9)?
owner_decisions.options:
(a) A netlify.toml rule for /deckcraft/plants/*: immutable Cache-Control and Content-Type model/gltf-binary.
- Every file there is content-hashed (GLBs and atlases, asserted by check-plant-species).
- species-manifest.json lives in scripts/ and is not served.
- Verified with curl -I on a deploy preview, never on production.
(b) Keep max-age=0 revalidation.

owner_decisions.question: D17: Mulch rings for trees planted in the lawn?
owner_decisions.options:
(a) None: an AO contact decal only (base radius + 10 in).
(b) A visual ring labelled 'not quoted'.
(c) An explicit 'add mulch ring' action that creates a real, quoted bed object.

owner_decisions.question:
D18: Sizes for newly placed plants (optional P10)?
Botany finds today's PLANT_LIBRARY envelopes are mature-ish, not as-installed:
- Trees: 180x108 in, against Ontario 50-60 mm caliper stock about 144-168 in tall with a 60-96 in crown.
- White pine: 168x96 in, against 60-80 in stock.
- Smaragd: 36 in wide, against 12-21 in.
- Shrubs: 36-48 in, against 18-30 in for #2-#3 pots.
- Perennials: 16-30 in, against 6-10 in for #1 pots.
Changing an envelope affects only newly placed plants. The showcase estate overrides several envelopes in showcaseSample.ts:286-309:
- Smaragd at 112x34 in three rows, and 140x48 in the mixed Smaragd/pine row.
- Maples and pines at 240x120, 230x110 and 200x100.
Library changes alone do not reach those rows.
owner_decisions.options:
(a) Keep the established look, and correct once only the proportions that are wrong at any age:
- Smaragd 96x36 to 96x24; maples 180x108 to 180x90; white pine 168x96 to 108x66; blue spruce 144x72 to 96x56.
- Also change the estate's Smaragd rows from 112x34 to 112x28. The mixed 140x48 row and the tree rows stay.
(a-lib) Same as (a), but leave the estate overrides untouched.
(b) Ontario installed sizes for new placements, plus an installed growth-stage model chosen at render time by the nearest saved heightIn.
(c) No change.
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a). Plans read as gardens rather than bare mulch, and the showcase stops displaying a too-fat Smaragd. Keep (b)'s growth stage as a later option.

owner_decisions.question: D19: When a user changes a plant's species, should its size reset to the new species' default? Today a hosta switched to sugar maple stays a 16x28 in maple.
owner_decisions.options:
(a) Yes, on that user action only, with no migration (P10). applySpecies moves to the Node-safe landscapeEdits.ts so it can be tested.
(b) No.

owner_decisions.question:
D20: The photo sourcing rule for iNaturalist CC0 inputs. Garden cultivars are graded casual (captive/cultivated), so research-grade alone finds nothing for several taxa. The review queried the API on 2026-10-17:
- Buxus microphylla: research 0, casual 55.
- Taxus × media: 0 at every grade.
- Hydrangea paniculata: research 0, casual 171.
- Calamagrostis × acutiflora: research 1.
owner_decisions.options:
(a) A per-taxon rule. The licence must be CC0 per photo, re-read at fetch time.
- Leaf and needle detail: species-level research-grade where at least 20 CC0 photos exist. Otherwise genus-level research-grade (Buxus 479, Taxus 2,508, Calamagrostis 2,447).
- H. paniculata, and every D6 cultivar colour target: casual-grade cultivated CC0, with the agent's identification check shown in the dry-run listing.
- Photos supply hue and chroma only.
(b) Research-grade species-level only. This fails for boxwood, yew, panicle hydrangea, Karl Foerster and every cultivar colour.
(c) No photos (D4b).
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a). The owner still approves each phase's exact list.

owner_decisions.question: D21: Live showcase on phones. 'Phones never see LOD0' holds only outside Showcase quality. The live 'Showcase quality' checkbox, the fly-through recorder and still export all force tier high (DPR 2, MSAA 4, 4096 shadows) and LOD0 for every plant, on any device.
owner_decisions.options:
(a) Gate only. Run the iPhone Showcase-quality fly-through at P3 and P9. If it loses context or its p95 is over 50 ms, apply a cap on narrow or touch devices: live showcase gives LOD0 to the nearest 40 plants and LOD1 to the rest. Still export is unchanged.
(b) Apply that cap now.
(c) No cap.
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a). The species models cut LOD0 to about 0.84M triangles with shared atlases, so the cap may never be needed. The gate proves it either way.

owner_decisions.question: D22: Variation between same-species plants (render-only). The estate has 76 Smaragd, 24 Karl Foerster, 21 hosta and 19 Annabelle.
owner_decisions.options:
(a) Render-only per-instance variation from plantColorHash: height ±5%, width ±7%, lean up to 3 degrees, plus yaw.
- Plus 2 seeded model variants at LOD0/LOD1 for Smaragd, Karl Foerster, hosta, Annabelle, serviceberry and dogwood, picked by object-id hash.
- On screen a plant can be up to 5% taller than its saved height; saved data, the MatureSpread ring and quotes are unchanged.
(b) Yaw and colour jitter only.
(c) Per-instance variation without extra model variants.
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a). Copy-paste repetition is the first CG tell a homeowner notices. The variants cost draws only at LOD0/LOD1, inside the P9 budgets.

owner_decisions.question: D23: Pre-approved performance contingencies, applied only when a phase's draw, overdraw or frame-time gate fails.
owner_decisions.options:
(a) Within that phase's PR, the agent may apply these steps in order, each shown with before/after metrics for owner review:
1. Drop the LOD1 variants.
2. Exclude LOD2 plant meshes from window-reflection passes. This edits windowReflections.ts but changes only which plants appear in reflections.
3. Merge per-role draws with BatchedMesh (three core, lazy chunk).
(b) Stop and ask the owner at each failure.
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a). It keeps a failed gate from stalling a wave, while every change is still reviewed before merge.
